Writing

Daily notes and the diary

A diary is the lowest-friction note there is: today already has a name, so there is nothing to decide before you start writing. Clew's diary is a calendar in the sidebar, a keystroke that always lands on today, and a choice of two honest storage shapes — one file per day, or one long log with a heading per day. On top of either shape it can compose read-only views of any stretch of time: today, this week, this month, or the entire diary rendered as a single continuous document.

The diary calendar

The diary lives in the Diary tab of the left sidebar: a month grid, Monday first, with a dot on every day that has an entry and today's date highlighted. The interactions are what you would guess:

  • Click a day to open its entry — or to create it, if the day is blank. There is no separate “new entry” step; the diary treats opening and creating as the same gesture.
  • The ‹ and › buttons step through months, and clicking the month name jumps back to the current month.
  • ⌘⇧D opens today's entry from anywhere, whether or not the panel is showing. The same command sits in the Go menu as Today's Diary Entry, next to Diary Calendar, which opens the panel itself.
  • From outside Clew, clew new --daily in a terminal or a clew://new?vault=…&daily=1 link does the same: see Links and the command line. (Not in 0.12.0.)

The dots track the vault live: create an entry by any route — the calendar, ⌘⇧D, or a file made by hand in the right folder with the right name — and the calendar picks it up.

Two ways to store a diary

Settings → Diary offers a Mode choice, and it is worth a moment's thought, because the two modes produce genuinely different vaults on disk. Both are plain Markdown; neither locks you in.

One note per day

The classic daily-notes shape: each day is its own file, named by the date format, inside the diary folder. With the defaults (folder Daily, format YYYY-MM-DD) a week of writing looks like this on disk:

On disk

Daily/
  2026-08-18.md
  2026-08-19.md
  2026-08-21.md
  2026-08-22.md

Days you skipped are files that never got created — the diary has no opinion about gaps. Per-day files suit a diary that accumulates substance: each day can grow its own headings, attachments, and backlinks, and each day is individually linkable as [[2026-08-22]].

A single log note

In log mode the whole diary is one note (by default Diary.md), and each day is a heading inside it, kept newest first:

On disk (Diary.md)

# 2026-08-22

Reviewed the draft; the second section still sags.

# 2026-08-21

Long walk. Nothing written, everything composted.

# 2026-08-19

Started reading the Fleck book.

Clicking a day in the calendar jumps straight to its section, creating the heading at the right chronological position if it does not exist yet. Any level-1 or level-2 heading whose text parses as a date in your configured format counts as a day; other headings are ordinary content inside the day above them. When the log is already open in an editor, Clew inserts the new section through that editor, so the insertion is undoable and never fights your unsaved edits. A log suits a diary of short entries — a line or three a day — where the pleasure is scrolling back through time in one file.

Note The diary settings are application-wide, not per-vault: the mode, folder, format, log file, and template apply to every vault you open. The entries themselves, of course, live in whichever vault you wrote them in.
Caution The date format must contain YYYY, MM, and DD — Clew needs to parse names back into dates to put dots on the calendar and order log sections. Any arrangement and separators work (DD.MM.YYYY, say), but in per-day mode the formatted date becomes a file name, so avoid characters that are not valid in file names, such as /.

Composed views: a week at a glance

Below the calendar sit the View buttons: Today, This week, This month, Everything, and Open interval with a pair of date pickers for any custom range. Each one gathers the requested days — files or log sections, whichever mode you are in — and composes them into a single document, newest first, which opens in a new tab in reading mode and is rendered by the full engine like any other note.

The composition is careful about structure: every day appears under a level-2 heading with its date, and any level-1 headings inside a daily note are demoted so the day headings remain the document's outline. The result reads as one continuous diary — this is the way to re-read a month, or to skim an entire year with Everything.

Caution A composed view is generated fresh each time and begins with a note saying so: edits made in the view are discarded the next time a view is generated. Write in the days themselves — the view is for reading. The view file lives at .clew/Diary View.md, invisible to the file explorer and the index, and view tabs are dropped when the app restarts.
Tip This week runs from Monday to today, which makes it a ready-made weekly review: open it Friday afternoon, read the week in one piece, and write the review entry for today while it is all in front of you.

Templates

A template is an ordinary note whose text seeds new content, with three placeholders substituted at insertion time:

PlaceholderBecomes
{{date}}Today's date, as YYYY-MM-DD.
{{date:FORMAT}}Today's date in a custom format — YYYY, MM, DD, HH, mm tokens, e.g. {{date:DD.MM.YYYY}}.
{{time}}The current time, as HH:mm.
{{time:FORMAT}}The current time in a custom format.
{{title}}The note's title — the formatted date for a diary entry, the note's name when inserting into an existing note.

Templates meet the diary through the Template note setting (Settings → Diary): name a note there and every newly created entry — a fresh per-day file, or a fresh section of the log — is seeded from it, placeholders substituted. A minimal daily template might be:

You write (the template note)

## {{date}} — plan

- [ ]

## Notes

Templates are not only for the diary. Insert Template… (⌘⌥T, or Format → Insert → Template…) lists every note in the Templates/ folder (the folder name is a setting) and inserts the chosen one at the cursor, with the same substitution — {{title}} becoming the current note's name. The demo vault ships one worked example, Templates/Meeting.md:

You write (Templates/Meeting.md)

---
tags: [meeting]
---
# {{title}} — {{date}}

Attendees:

## Notes

Create a note named after the meeting, press ⌘⌥T, choose Meeting, and the skeleton lands with the note's name and today's date already in the heading.

Tip Because the diary's template is resolved by name like a wikilink, keeping it in Templates/ gives you both behaviours from one file: it seeds new diary entries automatically and appears in the ⌘⌥T list for manual insertion elsewhere.
Obsidian compatibility Per-day files follow Obsidian's daily-notes convention — a folder of YYYY-MM-DD.md files — so an existing Obsidian daily-notes folder works as a Clew diary as-is, and entries written in Clew show up in Obsidian's daily notes. Clew never reads .obsidian/ settings, so set Clew's diary folder and date format to match what Obsidian uses. A single-log diary is plain Markdown headings that Obsidian renders happily, though Obsidian's own daily-notes machinery does not know about it. Composed views live under .clew/ and are invisible to Obsidian.

Reference

The diary's settings (Settings → Diary, plus the templates folder under Files):

SettingDefaultMeaning
ModeOne note per dayOne note per day or Single log note.
Log note (log mode)Diary.mdThe log file's path, in log mode.
Folder (per-day mode)DailyWhere per-day files live.
Date formatYYYY-MM-DDEntry names and log headings; must contain YYYY, MM, and DD.
Template note (optional)—A note whose text seeds every new entry.
Templates folderTemplatesWhere Insert Template… looks for templates.

Commands (all rebindable in the hotkey editor):

CommandHotkeyWhere
Open today's diary entry⌘⇧DGo menu, command palette.
Open diary calendar—Go menu, command palette, sidebar Diary tab.
Insert template…⌘⌥TFormat → Insert menu, command palette; needs an open editor.
